mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in three months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies pass on higher costs to consumers.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% in two months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which boosts the broader economy and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 2% in a month signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, which encourages risk-taking and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises by more than 0.3% in a month and nonfarm payrolls decrease by more than 100,000, it signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3% in 1 month AND PAYEMS decreases > 100,000
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% over three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate profit margins.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.
